title: TenirWsMessages
description: Single source of truth for the tenir WebSocket message contract between the clients (TS) and the FastAPI api (Python). TS types and Pydantic models are generated from this file; do not hand-edit the generated outputs. Audio is sent as raw BINARY WebSocket frames (16kHz, signed 16-bit little-endian, mono PCM); every JSON frame below is a control or result message.

MicSource.title: MicSource
MicSource.description: Which microphone the client is currently capturing from.

Lang.title: Lang
Lang.description: Languages the STT engine may detect/report on captions.

SessionStart.title: SessionStart
SessionStart.description: Client -> server. Opens a live session before any audio frames are sent.

sessionId.description: Optional client-provided id to resume a dropped session; the server echoes the authoritative id in session.ready.

MicSwitch.title: MicSwitch
MicSwitch.description: Client -> server. Runtime microphone source change.

SessionEnd.title: SessionEnd
SessionEnd.description: Client -> server. Finalizes the session; the transcript and retained audio are persisted.

Ping.title: Ping
Ping.description: Client -> server. Liveness probe; server replies with Pong.

t.description: Client send timestamp (ms epoch), echoed back.

SessionReady.title: SessionReady
SessionReady.description: Server -> client. Session accepted; client may begin streaming audio.

CaptionPartial.title: CaptionPartial
CaptionPartial.description: Server -> client. Fast, unstable hypothesis for the live caption band.

CaptionFinal.title: CaptionFinal
CaptionFinal.description: Server -> client. Stable finalized segment with timing.

Cue.title: Cue
Cue.description: Server -> client. A private contextual info card the api derived from the live conversation (e.g. someone asks how far the sun is; the answer appears). Cues are private to the listener, not part of the conversation. Clients show it in a bordered box above the live transcript for ~10s, and persist it inline in the transcript history at atMs.

cueId.description: Stable id for this cue (dedupe / popup keying).

title.description: 1-3 word label for the cue box.

body.description: The contextual detail shown in the box / history popup.

atMs.description: Position on the conversation timeline (ms) the cue relates to, so history can render it inline where it appeared.

source.description: Short label of the live source the cue's fact was grounded in (XERK-120), e.g. "BBC News" or "Wikipedia". Absent when the cue rests on the model's own knowledge; clients render it as a quiet attribution line under the body.

Translation.title: Translation
Translation.description: Server -> client. English translation of one finalized non-English turn (XERK-160). Delivered off the caption path once the turn's caption.final is out; clients pair it with that segment by segmentId (web/mobile/phone render it alongside the original turn, the glasses lens shows it in the cue box slot). While a translation run is live the api suppresses cues; the run ends with translation.done.

text.description: The English translation of the segment's text.

TranslationDone.title: TranslationDone
TranslationDone.description: Server -> client. The non-English run is over — the speaker is done being spoken-to in another language (an English turn arrived, or speech went quiet past the hold window). On the glasses this is what starts the translation box's 10s dismiss countdown; cue generation resumes after this.

LyricLine.title: LyricLine
LyricLine.description: One time-synced lyric line: the text and the timestamp (ms) it is sung at, measured from the START of the song (not the session).

atMs.description: Offset into the SONG (ms) at which this line is sung — the LRC timestamp.

text.description: The lyric line (may be empty for an instrumental gap).

Song.title: Song
Song.description: Server -> client. A song was recognized playing in the room (XERK-184). Clients show its time-synced lyrics in the same box a cue uses — title 'SONG NAME - ARTIST' over a body that auto-scrolls as the song plays. The scroll is driven client-side from an anchor: at session-timeline `atMs` the song was at `offsetMs` into the track, so the current line at wall-time t is the last line whose (song) atMs <= offsetMs + (t - atMs). A run of the same song is refreshed by `song.sync` and ended by `song.done`. While a song run is live the api suppresses cues, exactly as a translation run does.

songId.description: Stable id for this recognized-song run (keys song.sync / song.done / dedupe / history).

artist.description: The performing artist; the box title renders 'TITLE - ARTIST'.

atMs.description: The session-timeline position (ms) this anchor was measured at — where the song is placed in history, and the reference the client scrolls from.

offsetMs.description: How far into the SONG (ms) the track was at `atMs` — the sync anchor. Paired with atMs it maps wall-clock to song position.

durationMs.description: The track's total length (ms), when known; lets the client bound the scroll.

lines.description: The full time-synced lyrics (LRC), ordered by song time. Empty when no synced lyrics were found (the client shows the title without a scroll).

SongSync.title: SongSync
SongSync.description: Server -> client. A fresh sync anchor for a song already delivered (XERK-184): a periodic re-identification of the same run, so the client can correct drift between its local clock and the actual playback position. Carries no lyrics — same songId, same lines, new (atMs, offsetMs).

songId.description: The run this re-anchors (matches the Song's songId).

atMs.description: Session-timeline position of the fresh anchor.

offsetMs.description: Song position (ms) at the fresh anchor.

SongDone.title: SongDone
SongDone.description: Server -> client. The recognized song is over — it stopped matching past the hold window, or a different song took over (XERK-184). On the glasses this starts the song box's dismiss countdown, mirroring translation.done; cue generation resumes after it.

ErrorMessage.title: ErrorMessage
ErrorMessage.description: Server -> client. Recoverable or fatal error for the current session.
